note: True=agree-side key (SA/A); False=disagree-side (D/SD). Softened from 5-point Likert per Prickly prompt 21 Nov 2026.

items.text: A repository with 3,000 commits in the last year demonstrates that its maintainers write high-quality code.
If one contributor wrote over 90% of a project’s commits, that is a continuity risk worth reporting, though it does not by itself show the code is poor.
Cyclomatic complexity counts independent paths through a function; it indicates testing effort, not whether the function is correct.
Splitting a 40-branch function into two 20-branch functions that are always called together has reduced the system’s complexity.
If a project contains no benchmark results, the correct conclusion is that its performance is unknown, not that it is poor.
A function that ran 4% faster in one benchmark run than in the previous release’s single run is confirmed to have improved.
A claim that a change saves tokens should be backed by before-and-after token counts on the same workload.
A prompt change that cuts token usage by 30% has lowered the cost of the task, even if the answer error rate doubles.
A recorded execution trace lets an evaluator check which tools an agent called, in what order, and whether it looped.
If an agent’s final answer is correct, its execution path can be assumed to have been acceptable.
A domain-competency score is only meaningful relative to the reference dataset it was computed against.
Using the same questions to tune a system’s prompts and to report its final evaluation score gives an unbiased estimate of performance on new questions.
